item.description: The origin and early radiation of winged insects (Pterygota) represent one of the most transformative events in terrestrial evolution, yet phylogenetic relationships among their basalmost lineages (Ephemeroptera, Odonata and Neoptera) continue to be a central debate within insect systematics. Here, we present the most taxonomically comprehensive phylogenomic analysis to date, leveraging genomic and transcriptomic data from 101 species, including 16 sequenced ephemeropteran genomes. Employing 1,367 universal single-copy orthologs across two supermatrices, we used concatenation- and coalescent-based frameworks under homogeneous and heterogeneous, and multispecies coalescent models. Our analyses support Palaeoptera monophyly. Although coalescent-based methods initially suggested a Chiastomyaria (Ephemeroptera + Neoptera) topology, subsequent signal dissection and topology tests confirm that the preponderance of genomic signal favors a monophyletic Palaeoptera. Furthermore, we identify incomplete lineage sorting and gene tree estimation error as the primary drivers of previous topological conflicts. Our molecular dating results point to an Early Devonian origin of crown-Pterygota, whereas crown-Palaeoptera first emerged in the Late Devonian. By reconciling molecular evidence with morphological synapomorphies, such as wing-base sclerite homologies, this study provides a coherent framework for the early evolution of winged insects, supports a single origin of wings, and identifies the neopteran wing-folding mechanism as a singular evolutionary innovation. item.title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
item.dc:creator: Rikuto Fukushima
Masayuki Kano
Kazuro Hirahara
Makiko Ohtani
item.description: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. Agreement between model predictions and observations supports the hypothesis that observed slip diversity, including fast earthquakes and slow transient slips (Slow Slip Events; SSEs), originates from frictional heterogeneity. However, quantitative assessments of frictional heterogeneity from geodetic observations while fully incorporating fault mechanics are lacking due to the difficulties of high-dimensional optimization. In this study, we aim to address this gap using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to link frictional heterogeneity with geodetic observations. PINNs employ a neural network to represent the spatially variable frictional properties, making their estimation feasible. Targeting the 2010 Bungo SSE in southwest Japan, our estimation reveals heterogeneous friction coinciding with localized SSE nucleation in southwest Shikoku, and subsequent westward propagation. The calculated fault slip of SSE successfully reproduces the spatio-temporal pattern of observed surface displacements. This PINN-based inversion provides a mechanically consistent fault slip model validated through quantitative comparison with observations. Furthermore, we forecast the future fault slip evolution, demonstrating the importance of assimilating observations spanning multiple SSE cycles. Our results demonstrate the potential of PINN for advancing understanding of fault mechanics and enabling physics-based fault slip forecasting. Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan. item.description: Abstract Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. Geochemical parameters, methane plus sulfate profiles, and 16S rRNA gene-based bacterial diversity and community composition show partial convergence of the sediment-parameters to the translocated environment, suggesting climate change will rapidly alter bacteria communities of Baltic Sea coastal sediments. However, more pronounced responses in the control to the heated bay translocation direction suggest that while a return toward present-day conditions may be possible if climate change is reversed, such a recovery may be incomplete or require a longer time than one year. item.title: Onset of zircon decomposition during saprolitic weathering
item.dc:creator: Martin Yan Hei Li
Mei-Fu Zhou
item.description: Abstract Zircon is conventionally considered as refractory in supergene environments, enabling the preservation of geochemical records for tracing various Earth’s processes and the use of the zircon structure as a nuclear waste form. However, how refractory zircon is during weathering, especially when crystalline and in an early stage of weathering, is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that crystalline zircon would start to weather during an early-stage saprolitic weathering. Nano-scale examination reveals that weathering of zircon proceeds through dissolution of primary, crystalline zircon and precipitation of secondary, amorphous zircon. Non-formula elements, like U, Th and heavy rare earth elements, are uptake and structurally incorporated in this process. Thereby, metamictisation of the zircon would accelerate and eventually promote the dissolution of zircon. In supergene environments, zircon would steadily weather, calling for further evaluation on the geological and environmental applications of zircon. item.title: Hydrogen isotopes reveal water leakage from the core
item.dc:creator: Yu Zhang
Wenzhong Wang
Zhongqing Wu
Bowen Chen
item.description: Chemical heterogeneities in Earth’s deep mantle may record either preserved primordial reservoirs or later core-mantle exchange, but distinguishing between these origins remains challenging. Hydrogen isotopes offer a sensitive tracer, yet whether magma ocean crystallization could generate a deuterium-depleted deep reservoir has not been quantitatively evaluated. Here, we use machine learning–accelerated path-integral simulations to determine equilibrium hydrogen isotope fractionation between silicate melt and bridgmanite, ringwoodite, and wadsleyite under magma ocean conditions. Incorporating these fractionation factors into a magma ocean crystallization model shows that mineral-melt fractionation is intrinsically weak, producing an essentially homogeneous D/H distribution in the primitive mantle. Magma ocean crystallization therefore cannot generate the extremely low δD values observed in some ocean island basalts. Combined with exceptionally high 3 He/ 4 He ratios, these signatures more plausibly reflect selective transfer of primordial volatiles from Earth’s core, implying sustained volatile exchange across the core-mantle boundary. item.title: The riverine land-to-ocean carbon flux
item.dc:creator: Robert G. M. Spencer
Travis W. Drake
Maodian Liu
Peter A. Raymond
item.description: The land-to-ocean export of carbon via rivers is a key component in the global carbon cycle. In this Review, we provide an overview of the factors governing the mobilization of carbon into rivers and those modulating riverine carbon export to the ocean. Terrestrial landscapes are estimated to deliver 3–4 PgC yr^−1 to inland waters, with the majority outgassed rather than exported to the ocean. Model estimates converge on a total global carbon export flux of 0.8–1.0 PgC yr^−1; however, regional, watershed and carbon species resolved estimates vary substantially owing to differences in source inputs, transport processes, biogeochemical transformations, and climate and hydrological drivers. Across the models that were synthesized, global estimates for individual carbon species span approximately a threefold difference, whereas estimated export of some species to the Atlantic and Pacific basins varies by up to fivefold. The Amazon and Congo together contribute approximately 21% of global river discharge, yet remain far less observed than many smaller temperate watersheds; the world’s 30 largest rivers by discharge account for approximately half of global cumulative river discharge. Therefore, expanding observations is clearly a priority to reduce uncertainties in modelled land-to-ocean carbon fluxes, and could be supported by the development of sensor networks and remote sensing observations to improve spatiotemporal resolution. Integrating these large datasets with mechanistic studies of biogeochemical modulators and machine learning approaches would inform understanding of carbon dynamics within major watersheds and improve predictions of this globally important carbon flux. Globally, rivers export ~10^15 grams of carbon to the ocean each year. This Review explores the mobilization, modulation and transport of different species of carbon within watersheds and rivers, with the aim to help inform and improve land-to-ocean carbon flux estimates. item.dc:creator: Hugo Delile

item.description: How mining has shaped long-term economic and political landscapes across Europe and the Mediterranean remains poorly understood, largely because archaeological evidence is spatially fragmented and ore sources are difficult to trace from atmospheric lead (Pb) records. Here, we compile Pb isotope data from environmental archives and introduce the Environmental Match Intensity Index (EMII), a metric applied to peat records to track Pb–silver (Ag) ore-supply patterns and relative changes in the integrated mining-related atmospheric Pb signal over six millennia. EMII reveals an early mining signal centered on Laurion (Greece) during the Late Neolithic/Chalcolithic, followed by Bronze Age expansion structured by maritime routes linking the Cyclades, the Troad, and Anatolian coasts. From the Iron Age onward, our results challenge the conventional Iberian-centered mining model and instead reveal a polycentric and multimodal organization rooted in west-central European districts interconnected through major fluvial corridors and complementary terrestrial and maritime routes. EMII reaches its first major peak during the Early Roman period, declines during Late Antiquity and the Early Middle Ages, and rises again from the High Middle Ages onward. Despite these temporal fluctuations, the overall continental distribution of the contributing mining regions remains broadly stable. By connecting environmental archives with mining, transport, and urban demand, this framework provides a scalable approach for reconstructing the long-term organization of metal production and circulation and their contribution to anthropization processes across different chrono-cultural periods and geographical settings. item.description: The giant Jiaojia gold deposit (>200 t Au) in the Jiaodong Peninsula, China, hosts three distinct mineralization styles: disseminated, breccia, and stockwork (orebodies I and II); thin pyrite-muscovite-quartz veins (orebody III); and auriferous quartz-sulfide veins (orebody IV). These styles are spatially controlled by a multiorder fault network. Integrated in situ textural, trace-element, and sulfur isotope analyses of pyrite reveal that these styles formed during a single hydrothermal event, with gold precipitation mechanisms varying systematically with structural setting. In the high-strain fault core and damage zone of the Jiaojia fault zone (orebodies I and II), extensive fluid-rock interaction and sulfidation dominated, producing pyrite enriched in Ag, As, Au, Bi, Cu, Pb, Sb, and Te, with heavier δ34S values (median 10.95‰) relative to those in orebodies III and IV. In contrast, steep faults within the secondary Baoli fault zone hosting orebody IV record lighter δ34S values (median 9.48‰) and porous pyrite with elevated Au/As ratios and broad trace-element variability, indicating rapid crystallization from fluids that underwent intense phase separation triggered by abrupt pressure drops. Orebody III, hosted in the transitional zone, displays mixed geochemical and isotopic characteristics, reflecting contributions from both sulfidation and phase separation. Overlapping homogenization temperatures of fluid inclusions from previous studies across orebodies rule out significant thermal gradients, demonstrating that fault zone architecture, by modulating sulfidation and fluid depressurization, was the primary control on gold precipitation. item.description: Abstract We integrate major and trace element data with high-precision Pb isotope analyses of ores from the Middle Miocene felsic volcanic-hosted massive sulfide deposits of northeast Japan, including the Matsumine-Shakanai, Furutobe, and Nurukawa deposits, to elucidate the distribution and source of precious metals. Gold and Ag are hosted mainly by sulfosalts at Matsumine-Shakanai but occur predominantly as electrum at Furutobe and Nurukawa. The uranogenic 207 Pb/ 204 Pb vs. 206 Pb/ 204 Pb plot defines distinct clusters with a steep linear trend, indicating two metal source components: a relatively unradiogenic, juvenile source corresponding to the Middle Miocene volcanic rocks and a more radiogenic source attributed to pre-Miocene basement rocks. At Matsumine-Shakanai, correlations between 207 Pb/ 204 Pb and Zn, Pb, Au, and Ag suggest a dominant contribution from evolved basement rocks for these metals. Such relationships are absent at Furutobe and Nurukawa, suggesting that Au and Ag enrichments at these deposits were controlled by other processes, such as transport and depositional processes. Lead isotope maps reveal a north-south trend parallel to the Miocene fault systems, reflecting hydrothermal fluid pathways. Incorporating recent findings of petrological studies on the thermal evolution of volcanic host rocks, we propose a geological model that involves progressive heating of the shallow crust in an extensional setting, which resulted in rising of the isotherms and extraction of metals from an isotopically evolved source providing much of Zn, Au, and Ag and an isotopically juvenile source providing Cu. item.description: The transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision is a key mechanism for understanding orogenic architecture and continental crustal growth. Within this framework, the geodynamic evolution of the Neo-Tethyan slab remains a subject of intensive debate concerning the formation of the Tibetan Plateau. Both dyke suites were emplaced at 47–46 Ma and exhibit subduction-related arc affinities. Zircons from the diorite-porphyry and granite dykes have positive εHf(t) values of +9.0 to +11.2 and +11.9 to +13.8, respectively. The diorite-porphyry dykes exhibit high Mg#, Cr, Ni and adakitic characteristics, which indicate their derivation from partial melting of the subducted Neo-Tethyan slab followed by interaction with the overlying mantle peridotite. In contrast, the granite dykes were derived from the melting of juvenile crust and dominantly underwent fractional crystallization of K-feldspar and plagioclase. The spatiotemporal distribution of regional magmatic records, characterized by an overall eastward-younging trend, is consistent with diachronous eastward propagation of Neo-Tethyan slab breakoff. The coexistence of these two dyke suites provides evidence for slab-window development beneath the central segment of the southern Lhasa subterrane at approximately 47 Ma. item.description: Subduction initiation is a fundamental geodynamic process in plate tectonics, yet its mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the scarcity of geological records. Proposed geological records of subduction initiation, including metamorphic soles, fore-arc basalts and fore-arc sediments, are typically associated with spontaneous subduction initiation in hot environments involving mantle upwelling. In contrast, evidence for the more common cold subduction initiation at continental margins is sparse or even absent. Arc volcanic rocks are widely regarded as direct evidence of subduction zones, particularly for identifying ancient subduction zones in orogens. However, the temporal relationship between subduction initiation and the onset of arc volcanism remains poorly constrained. Although arc volcanism is generally considered to develop within ∼10 million years (Myr) of initiation, our analysis of subduction events over the past 15 Myr reveals a highly variable time lag ranging from 2 to 10 Myr. In this study, we investigate the factors controlling this time lag in forced subduction initiation at continental margins, using a newly developed two-phase flow numerical model that incorporates melt transport and melt extraction processes. Our results show that rapid partial melting at shallow depths, primarily driven by high convergence rates, leads to a shorter time lag between subduction initiation and arc volcanism, which is consistent with observations from recent subduction events. These findings suggest that arc volcanic rocks, when considered together with slab age and convergence rate, provide a useful constraint on the timing of subduction initiation in ancient subduction systems. item.description: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Numerous studies have investigated its stable metal isotope character to understand its formation and secular evolution. Here, we report high-precision whole-rock Mo isotope data for 28 Archean granitoids from Australia’s Pilbara and Yilgarn cratons, with crystallization ages from 3.52 to 2.63 Ga. The samples cover a spectrum of magmatic series, including tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG), TTG hybrid, sanukitoid, potassic, and potassic hybrid magmas. After assessing the effects of alteration, crustal contamination, and fluid exsolution, we interpret the observed δ 98/95Mo range of − 0.93 to 0.25‰ as primarily reflecting magmatic source characteristics. TTG and TTG hybrid granitoids, together with samples derived from unenriched meta-mafic or mantle-like sources, have mean and median δ 98/95Mo values close to, or slightly higher than, chondrite and depleted MORB mantle (DMM). In contrast, potassic, potassic hybrid, and sanukitoid series granitoids, as well as samples derived from enriched meta-mafic or felsic crustal sources, extend to lower, sub-mantle δ 98/95Mo values. Elemental proxy relationships, major- and trace-element modeling, and phase-equilibrium constraints indicate that source composition and residual mineralogy during partial melting primarily control Mo isotope variability in these rocks. In crustally-derived granitoids, lower δ 98/95Mo values are associated with more mature source compositions and with changes in the abundance and composition of residual feldspar. Amphibole, garnet, and biotite may also have subordinate effects. These relationships suggest that Mo isotopes track the progressive reworking of Archean crust. Juvenile crust-derived TTG magmatism is characterized by near- to suprachondritic δ 98/95Mo, whereas later sanukitoid and potassic granitoid magmatism, linked respectively to mantle metasomatism and reworking of TTG-dominated gray gneiss, shifts toward lower δ 98/95Mo values. The observed trends imply that intracrustal reworking alone can push continental averages to sub-mantle values, with ramifications for mass-balance models. Although TTGs are generally suprachondritic, their δ 98/95Mo values are not high enough to easily support models requiring large volumes of Hadean to Paleoarchean continental extraction from a chondritic mantle to offset the subchondritic Mo isotope composition inferred for the depleted mantle from Archean komatiites. The strong Mo isotope contrast between continental crust and upper mantle may therefore have developed after 2.6 Ga, once crustal recycling became more extensive. item.description: The West Qinling gold metallogenic province is one of China’s largest gold producers, yet the genesis and temporal framework of its gold deposits remain highly debated. Variable bell-shape REE patterns and positive correlations between EuN and Eu* in scheelite indicate an oxidizing environment, controlled by variations in fluid salinity and Na-REE coupled substitution mechanism. Fluid inclusion microthermometry of coexisting scheelite and quartz shows consistent homogenization temperatures (163–307 ℃) and salinity (0.7–19.13 wt% NaCl equiv), implying a shared fluid origin. These findings provide new constraints on the origin of the Huachanggou gold deposit and establish scheelite as a robust indicator for orogenic gold exploration. Regionally, the ca. 219–209 Ma link mineralization to post-collisional crustal reworking in the West Qinling, offering a temporal framework for targeting similar deposits in convergent-margin settings worldwide. item.description: Kimberlites and related CO2-rich ultramafic rocks such as aillikites commonly show Nd-Hf isotope decoupling (unradiogenic εHf at a given εNd), attributed to either recycled oceanic slabs or interaction with metasomatized continental lithospheric mantle (CLM). The Nd-Hf isotope decoupling in aillikites and kimberlites therefore records interaction between deep CO2-rich melts and ancient CLM domains. Primitive CO2-rich intraplate magmatism, especially in cratonic settings, offers unique insights into deep carbon cycling and the fate of CO2-rich melts on their way to Earth’s surface. item.description: The Söğüt gold deposit in northwestern Anatolia represents one of Türkiye's significant recent gold discoveries. The deposit is structurally controlled by E–W-trending, south-vergent shear zones and is characterised by gold-bearing mineral assemblages, including native gold, native tellurium, coloradoite, calaverite, stibnite, and scheelite. Mineralisation is associated with pervasive Mg–Fe-rich alteration dominated by carbonate minerals, particularly dolomite, ankerite, and siderite. Despite its economic significance and distinctive mineral assemblage, the timing, physicochemical conditions, and mechanisms responsible for gold mineralisation at Söğüt have remained poorly constrained. Here, we investigate the genetic evolution of the Söğüt deposit by integrating ore mineralogy, carbonate alteration, sulphur isotope compositions of pyrite, fluid-inclusion microthermometry, and geochronological constraints. The results indicate that mineralisation formed at approximately 375 °C and 1.6 kbar from low-salinity, CO₂-bearing metamorphic fluids. We propose that episodic reactivation of the controlling shear zones caused transient pressure fluctuations and promoted fluid immiscibility, which together with wall-rock sulphidation and carbonatization, destabilised aqueous gold–bisulphide complexes and facilitated gold precipitation. Systematic variations in in-situ δ34S values of pyrite, ranging from negative values in the early mineralising stage (−8.64 to −3.65‰) to positive values in late-stage barren pyrite (+11.39 to +13.93‰), reflect an evolving metamorphic fluid system that acquired sulphur from metasedimentary protoliths and subsequently underwent progressive sulphur depletion and fluid mixing. We further link the timing and genesis of the Söğüt mineralisation to Paleocene continental collision in northwestern Anatolia. The ca. 58 Ma mineralisation broadly overlaps Barrovian metamorphism (ca. 64–57 Ma) of the Tavşanlı Zone during its underthrusting beneath the Sakarya margin, providing a temporal and tectonic framework for metamorphic fluid generation and hydrothermal activity in the overriding plate. Slab break-off and associated asthenospheric upwelling may have enhanced the regional thermal regime but are not required as the direct trigger for mineralisation. item.description: Since the India-Eurasia continental collision, the Tethyan Himalaya has undergone distinctive tectono-magmatic events, including the emplacement of leucogranites and the development of the South Tibetan Detachment System (STDS). These processes have generated a series of Pb-Zn-Sb-Au deposits that are closely tied to tectono-magmatic activity. However, the spatiotemporal relationships between structures, magmatism, and mineralization, as well as the pathways for fluid migration, remain poorly constrained. This gap in understanding has impeded both the development of a robust metallogenic theory and the deployment of effective exploration strategies. This study focuses on the Zhaxikang Pb-Zn-Sb polymetallic deposit, the largest and most extensively studied deposit in the belt. We integrate multi-scale geophysical surveys, carbonaceous Raman spectroscopy thermometry, and 40Ar-39Ar geochronology to achieve the following objectives: (1) construct a comprehensive spatiotemporal framework linking the deposit to regional structures and magmatism; (2) delineate the ore-forming fluid migration pathways; and (3) propose a new metallogenic model and exploration approach. Our results demonstrate that:(1) A low-resistivity, low-density, partially molten layer exists at a depth of 10–15 km beneath Zhaxikang. The east–west trending regional fault F1-1 directly connects this deep molten layer to the shallow orebody, forming a vertical fluid transport system. (2) A multi-scale fault network (F1-2 throw ≈ 1.67 km, F2-2 throw ≈ 1.44 km, F3-1 throw ≈ 328 m, V ore vein throw ≈ 172–326 m) controls long-distance, multi-stage fluid migration. (3) The 40Ar-39Ar age of muscovite from the F1-1 fault (18.9 Ma) is highly consistent with the main Sb mineralization stage in the ore cluster (17.9–12.2 Ma), confirming this fault’s key role in ore formation. Based on these results, we propose a “Zhaxikang-type” tectono-magmatic coupling metallogenic model. In this model, persistent partial melting, coupled with multi-stage fault activity, generates a “seismic pump” suction effect. This mechanism drives ore-forming fluids to migrate over long distances through an interconnected, multi-level fault network, resulting in the multi-stage mineralization observed at Zhaxikang from 43.1 Ma to the present. Following this theoretical framework, we traced the fluid migration path and detected a concealed ore vein (VIe) anomaly 750 m east of the Ve ore vein, successfully completing a loop from theoretical construction to exploration verification. item.description: Continuous Cenozoic India-Asia convergence and collision has formed the Himalayan orogen with complex multiphase structural deformation, magmatism and metamorphism, preserving critical records for unraveling the Himalayan orogenic process and collisional orogeny. This paper reviews the records of tectonics, anatexis, magmatism, metamorphism and uplift history of typical localities in the orogen, with a focus on the mid-Miocene geological processes. It is concluded that the delamination of Indian lithospheric mantle triggered the (ultra-) high temperature anatexis-magmatic-metamorphic events and rapid uplift of the orogen in the mid-Miocene. The removal of the orogenic root reduced the resistance to underthrusting, induced the (re-) activation of the thrusts, and rejuvenated the Himalayan orogenesis, with its influence in Tibet and its adjacent regions. item.title: Magmatic evolution and Fe-Ti oxide layer formation in the Panzhihua intrusion: Roles of magma replenishment and density-driven sorting in remobilized crystal slurries

item.description: The Panzhihua intrusion is a late Permian layered gabbroic sill within the Emeishan Large Igneous Province and hosts significant magmatic Fe–Ti–V oxide deposits. Despite extensive study, the magmatic processes controlling the evolution of the intrusion and its associated Fe-Ti oxide mineralization remain poorly understood. Here, we show that multiple upward reversals in clinopyroxene Mg# and plagioclase An in the Lower Zone (LZ) record repeated replenishment by primitive magma, which mixed with resident evolved melt and renewed crystallization of Mg-rich clinopyroxene, calcic plagioclase, and Fe-Ti oxides. In contrast, monotonic upward decreases in clinopyroxene Mg# and plagioclase An through the Middle Zone a (MZa) reflect diminishing magma replenishment and increasing fractional crystallization. Ilmenite/magnetite (Ilm/Mt) ratios increase from 0:100–10:90 in the LZ to 5:95–25:75 in the MZa, accompanied by higher whole-rock TiO2/Fe2O3T ratios and lower Fe3+/Ti4+ ratios, indicating progressively greater ilmenite crystallization. MELTS modeling further supports cotectic crystallization of Fe-Ti oxides and silicate minerals from an oxidized, high-Ti parental magma. Using a magnetite–clinopyroxene vanadium oxybarometer, we obtained oxygen fugacity estimates of approximately QFM + 1.5 ± 0.2 log units (1 SD) for both the LZ and MZa. Systematic along-strike variations in LZ thickness and whole-rock composition, together with rhythmic modal layering, planar foliation, and mineral lineation, provide evidence for large-scale lateral redistribution of crystal slurries and density-driven mineral sorting during magmatic evolution. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the architecture and Fe-Ti oxide mineralization of the Panzhihua intrusion were governed by the combined effects of repeated magma replenishment, fractional crystallization, and large-scale lateral redistribution and density sorting of crystal slurries.
